newsitem.title: USA: KCPL, Western Resources to merge.
newsitem.headline: KCPL, Western Resources to merge.

text.p: Kansas City Power and Light Co. and Western Resources Inc. will merge in a $2 billion stock swap, Western Resources announced Friday, declaring victory in its hostile bid for the utility.
Under the tax-free deal, Kansas City Power and Light shareholders will receive $32 worth of Western Resources stock for each share they hold.
The deal is believed to be the first successful hostile takeover among U.S. utilities.

Kansas City Power's surrender -- which came after Western Resources sweetened its bid to $32 a share from $31 after long negotiations -- ended a 10-month battle in which UtiliCorp United Inc.'s friendly pact to merge with Kansas City Power fell apart after its shareholders failed in September to back the less lucrative offer.

Analysts have said the merger would create a Midwestern electric and natural gas powerhouse better poised to compete in the deregulating utility business. The merged company will have nearly $3 billion in annual revenues and nearly 2.5 million gas and electric customers. Western Resources also has 430,000 security customers.

Under the deal, John Hayes, chief executive of Topeka, Kan.-based Western Resources, will remain chief executive and chairman of the new company, while Kansas City Power Chief Executive Drue Jennings will become vice chairman. The deal is subject to approval by state and federal regulatory bodies and the shareholders of both companies.
